paragraphs.text: Stirling IV LK276 of 190 Squadron flew from Great Dunmow (Newton Field) on a night glider-towing sortie on 20/21 November 1944. It was towing Horsa glider P-F573 with Flying Officer Brain aboard as check pilot. The glider was released at 21:08 and landed safely. At 21:13 the pilot asked to land and was told to hold off and circle the outer perimeter lights. At 21:20 the Stirling hit willow trees and high-tension cables, skidded along a bank and exploded. All seven crew died. Local reporting places the impact in the field where Great Dunmow Primary School now stands.

The cause is disputed. Aircrew Remembered says the board of enquiry blamed the pilot for failing to monitor his altimeter, and also reports later investigations that a Luftwaffe night fighter shot the aircraft down. The rafweb casualty listing says it may have been shot down by an enemy intruder. The bench plaques for Dauncey, Woods and Holt say the crash was the result of enemy action; that is the plaque wording, not a verified finding.

The seven crew were Flying Officer James Ian Kidgell (pilot, RAAF, 23), Flying Officer William Walter D'Arcy Brain (second pilot and instructor, RNZAF, 26), Flying Officer Ernest Douglas Woods (navigator, 26), Sergeant Hugh Holt (flight engineer, 20), Flight Sergeant Ronald David Payne (air bomber, 21), Flight Sergeant Reginald Matthew Dauncey (wireless operator and air gunner, 23) and Flight Sergeant Arthur George Reid (air gunner, 33). Kidgell, Brain and Reid are buried at Brookwood Military Cemetery; Woods at Chapeltown, Holt at Burnley, Payne at Lewisham and Dauncey at Northwich.

A large freestanding stone with a bronze plaque naming the seven crew stands in the gardens at Easton Lodge, Little Easton. The IWM register lists seven names, all of men who died, and records the stone and plaque in good condition. It does not state who made the stone or when it was dedicated, and the site is Grade II listed.

Great Dunmow Town Council erected seven benches in the town, one for each crew member, and the final ceremony was held on 21 November 2010, with relatives attending. The sources read do not say who looks after the Little Easton stone.

notes: CUSTODIAN UNKNOWN: IWM 97203 gives no maker, date or maintainer for the Little Easton stone; no source found saying who erected or looks after it (gardens are Grade II listed, run separately; not confirmed as custodian). Leads: Easton Lodge Gardens owners, Kidgell/Chaplin book 'The Seven Airmen of Stirling LK276' (2019), Dunmow Town Council. Not made claims: nationality for Woods, Holt, Payne, Dauncey and Reid (no source read states it; our record says British); IBCC and CWGC links for six of seven men (CWGC and IBCC pages blocked or unsearchable by name; only Kidgell's CWGC ID 2667301 from IWM 97194, URL pattern copied from an existing dossier and unverified). Aircrew Remembered is internally inconsistent (six killed at scene, rear gunner died of injuries, seven listed dead); crash dated 20/21 Nov there, 21 Nov elsewhere. Crash site: Aircrew Remembered says 'Puildings Farm'; Dunmow Broadcast says field of the primary school / Newton Green. Dunmow Broadcast (secondary) also says the landing lights were switched off because an unidentified aircraft was detected; not used in text as single-source. IWM bench dedication dates are inconsistent (2000/2007/2010) and the 2000 entries predate the 2010 article. Holt's first plaque age (33) was wrong. The IWM 'Easton Lodge Stirling Walk' obelisk (190 and 620 Sqns, 9 June 2000, Waymarking) is a different memorial. No photos included: IWM photos were not in research/iwm capture for these ids. Sources S4-S11 are all IWM (one publisher). Dunmow Broadcast is quoted partly via IWM so is not treated as independent of it.
